headline: High-risk orchestration pair: Kestra’s broad write/network defaults can cascade errors and leak data when paired with a read-only game agent, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the game agent’s lack of ingestion surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no ingestion or shared channel, and network_egress is none. kestra can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so a manual or file-based bridge is possible, but the pair lacks a documented default path where godot_rl_agents consumes Kestra output as instructions. Risk stays low.
conditions: IF an operator copies Kestra output into a file or stdin that godot_rl_agents parses as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace is introduced between the two agents, prompt content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe Kestra stdout into any prompt or config consumed by godot_rl_agents.
Use explicit human review before copying outputs between agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data, and it has broad network egress plus file access. godot_rl_agents is read-only from the profile side, but if it is pointed at the same workspace or artifacts, Kestra can expose sensitive workflow data to the pair’s outputs. The shared-data pathway is plausible in default orchestration setups.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same /app/storage or /tmp tree, Kestra-managed data can be read by the pair.
IF Kestra workflows include secrets in logs or artifacts, those values can flow into downstream outputs.
mitigations: Separate storage mounts for each agent.
Redact secrets from Kestra logs and artifacts.
Restrict Kestra network egress to approved destinations.
Review shared-file permissions before running both agents.
requires-engineering: add per-artifact access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no write surfaces, but kestra can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, write the filesystem, and supports multiple instances. If both are pointed at the same directory or repo, Kestra’s default mutability can overwrite or race with files the game agent relies on. Uncertainty is limited by the explicit write capability on Kestra and absence of isolation on the pair boundary.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory, file clobbering or race conditions can occur.
IF Kestra workflows modify git or shared artifacts without locks, concurrent runs can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Disable concurrent Kestra runs on shared paths.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
Run Kestra with least-privilege filesystem access.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kestra is an automation/orchestration system that can act on workflow outputs via HTTP, email, Slack, cloud, and other tasks. If it consumes godot_rl_agents output as authoritative, a bad game-agent result can cascade into real actions. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so the safer assumption is that downstream automation may trust upstream output.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows use godot_rl_agents output as an input to notifications or actions without validation, errors can propagate.
IF the game agent emits incorrect state or recommendations, Kestra can operationalize them into downstream tasks.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before action tasks.
Validate agent output against schema and invariants.
Limit Kestra to dry-run mode for new workflows.
Log and diff upstream outputs before execution.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented in either profile, and godot_rl_agents touches no data classes. Kestra does handle logs, inputs, artifacts, and cloud/database data, so compliance concerns exist only if regulated data is routed through it. The pair itself does not prove a breach, so this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through Kestra workflows, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency requirements differ across downstream systems, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair.
Document data residency for Kestra-connected services.
Set short log retention on Kestra.
Review downstream certifications before enabling sensitive workflows.
